subject: maths
title: Decimal Calculations
seo_title: Year 6 Decimal Calculations Worksheets: × and ÷ by 10, 100, 1,000, Short Multiplication and Division with Decimals
standard_text: Multiply and divide numbers by 10, 100 and 1,000 giving answers up to three decimal places; multiply one-digit numbers with up to two decimal places by whole numbers; use written division methods in cases where the answer has up to two decimal places; solve problems which require answers to be rounded to specified degrees of accuracy.
meta_desc: Free Year 6 maths worksheets on decimal calculations for the National Curriculum and KS2 SATs: multiply and divide by 10, 100 and 1,000, add and subtract decimals, short multiplication and short division with decimal answers, rounding, and money and measure problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: The digits move, the decimal point stays still. Line up the points to add and subtract, and keep the point in line when you multiply and divide.
body_html:
Multiply and divide by 10, 100 and 1,000

The digits move; the decimal point stays still. Multiplying moves every digit to the left. Dividing moves every digit to the right: 1 place for 10, 2 places for 100, 3 places for 1,000. Fill empty places up to the ones with 0.

Example

0.037 × 1,000

Each digit moves 3 places to the left. The 3 goes to the tens and the 7 to the ones.

Answer: 37

Add and subtract: line up the points

Use column addition and column subtraction. Line up the decimal points, not the last digits. Write zeros in empty places so every column has a digit.

Multiply a decimal by a whole number

Use short multiplication. Start with the smallest place. The point in the answer goes straight below the point in the question.

Estimate first: 2.45 is about 2.5, and 2.5 × 6 = 15. So 14.7 makes sense; 1.47 and 147 do not.

Divide: keep going past the point

Use short division. When there is a remainder, write the point and zeros after the number and keep dividing. The point in the answer goes straight above the point in the number.

Round to the accuracy you are asked for

Work out one more place than you need. Then look at that digit: 5 or more, round up; 4 or less, round down. Money is rounded to the nearest penny (2 decimal places).

Example

£10 is shared equally by 3 people. How much does each get, to the nearest penny?

10 ÷ 3 = 3.333… The third decimal place is 3, so round down.

Answer: £3.33

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
4.6 ÷ 100 = 0.46 or 0.0046÷ 100 moves the digits exactly 2 places: 0.046
4.6 × 10 = 4.60 (adding a zero)The digits move 1 place left: 46
Lining up the last digits: 4.7 + 1.25 = 1.72Line up the points: 4.70 + 1.25 = 5.95
2.45 × 6 = 147 or 1.470Keep the point in line: 14.70 = 14.7
17 ÷ 4 = 4.1 (remainder written as a decimal)Write 17.00 and keep dividing: 4.25
Rounding 3.45 to 1 decimal place as 3.4The hundredths digit is 5, so round up: 3.5

faq.q: What decimal calculations are in the Year 6 SATs?
faq.a: The arithmetic paper has questions like 12.5 − 3.78, 2.45 × 6, 4.6 ÷ 100 and 9.36 ÷ 3, and the reasoning papers use decimals in money and measure problems, sometimes with answers rounded to a given accuracy.

faq.q: How do you divide a whole number to get a decimal answer?
faq.a: Use short division and do not stop at the remainder. Write a decimal point and zeros after the number, exchange the remainder into tenths and hundredths and keep dividing: 17 ÷ 4 = 17.00 ÷ 4 = 4.25.

faq.q: How do you multiply a decimal by a whole number in Year 6?
faq.a: Use short multiplication, starting with the smallest place and exchanging as usual, and put the decimal point in the answer straight below the point in the question. 2.45 × 6 = 14.70, which is 14.7.

faq.q: Does the decimal point move when you multiply by 10?
faq.a: In English schools children are taught that the digits move and the decimal point stays still. When you multiply by 10 each digit moves one place to the left, so 3.42 × 10 = 34.2.

items.e: 4.6 ÷ 100: every digit moves 2 places to the right. The decimal point stays still. Write 0 in the empty places up to the ones. 4.6 ÷ 100 = 0.046.
0.37 × 10: every digit moves 1 place to the left. The decimal point stays still. 0.37 × 10 = 3.7.
2.58 × 100: every digit moves 2 places to the left. The decimal point stays still. 2.58 × 100 = 258.
6.1 × 1,000: every digit moves 3 places to the left. The decimal point stays still. Write 0 in the empty places up to the ones. 6.1 × 1,000 = 6,100.
52 ÷ 1,000: every digit moves 3 places to the right. The decimal point stays still. Write 0 in the empty places up to the ones. 52 ÷ 1,000 = 0.052.
0.4 ÷ 10: every digit moves 1 place to the right. The decimal point stays still. Write 0 in the empty places up to the ones. 0.4 ÷ 10 = 0.04.
0.008 × 100: every digit moves 2 places to the left. The decimal point stays still. 0.008 × 100 = 0.8.
309 ÷ 100: every digit moves 2 places to the right. The decimal point stays still. 309 ÷ 100 = 3.09.
7.25 ÷ 10: every digit moves 1 place to the right. The decimal point stays still. Write 0 in the empty places up to the ones. 7.25 ÷ 10 = 0.725.
0.06 × 1,000: every digit moves 3 places to the left. The decimal point stays still. Write 0 in the empty places up to the ones. 0.06 × 1,000 = 60.
13.4 ÷ 100: every digit moves 2 places to the right. The decimal point stays still. Write 0 in the empty places up to the ones. 13.4 ÷ 100 = 0.134.
0.045 × 1,000: every digit moves 3 places to the left. The decimal point stays still. 0.045 × 1,000 = 45.
Use the inverse: 0.32 × 100. The digits move 2 places to the left: 32. Check: 32 ÷ 100 = 0.32.
The 4 moved from the ones to the thousands: that is 3 places to the left, so the number is 1,000. (4.5 × 100 = 450.)
The 1 moved from the tens to the hundredths: that is 3 places to the right, so it is ÷ 1,000. (18 ÷ 100 = 0.18.)

items.q: Which calculation has the answer 0.63?
The chart shows 70.5 ÷ 100 = 0.705. What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: 70.5 ÷ 100 = 0.705. Every digit moved 2 places to the right, so the 5 is now in the thousandths place. Its value is 5 thousandths.

items.q: The chart shows 3.42 × 10 = 34.2. What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: 3.42 × 10 = 34.2. Every digit moved 1 place to the left, so the 4 is now in the ones place. Its value is 4 ones.

items.q: The chart shows 86 ÷ 1,000 = 0.086. What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: 86 ÷ 1,000 = 0.086. Every digit moved 3 places to the right, so the 8 is now in the hundredths place. Its value is 8 hundredths.

items.q: The chart shows 0.29 × 100 = 29. What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: 0.29 × 100 = 29. Every digit moved 2 places to the left, so the 2 is now in the tens place. Its value is 2 tens.

items.q: Use column addition. The grey zeros fill the empty places.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 2.6 as 2.60 so every place has a digit. 3.45 + 2.60 = 6.05.

items.q: Use column subtraction. The grey zeros fill the empty places.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 12.5 as 12.50 so every place has a digit. 12.50 − 3.78 = 8.72. Check with the inverse: 8.72 + 3.78 = 12.5.

items.q: Use column addition. The grey zeros fill the empty places.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 7.8 as 7.80 so every place has a digit. 7.80 + 0.56 = 8.36.

items.q: Use column subtraction. The grey zeros fill the empty places.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 8 as 8.00 so every place has a digit. 8.00 − 2.35 = 5.65. Check with the inverse: 5.65 + 2.35 = 8.

items.q: Use column addition. The grey zeros fill the empty places.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 14.3 as 14.30 so every place has a digit. 14.30 + 2.95 = 17.25.

items.q: Use column subtraction. The grey zeros fill the empty places.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 3.7 as 3.70 so every place has a digit. 9.06 − 3.70 = 5.36. Check with the inverse: 5.36 + 3.7 = 9.06.

items.q: Arjun worked out 4.7 + 1.25 like this. What is the correct answer?
items.e: Arjun lined up the last digits, so the 7 tenths were added to 5 hundredths. Line up the decimal points: 4.70 + 1.25 = 5.95. (5.32 puts the 7 in the hundredths column.)
Line up the decimal points. Write 0.6 as 0.60 so every place has a digit. 0.75 + 0.60 = 1.35.
Line up the decimal points. Write 3.9 as 3.90 so every place has a digit. 6.07 + 3.90 = 9.97.
Line up the decimal points. Write 10 as 10.00 so every place has a digit. 10.00 − 4.62 = 5.38. Check with the inverse: 5.38 + 4.62 = 10.
Line up the decimal points. Write 5.3 as 5.30 so every place has a digit. 5.30 − 0.86 = 4.44. Check with the inverse: 4.44 + 0.86 = 5.3.
Line up the decimal points. Write 15 as 15.00 so every place has a digit. 15.00 − 6.25 = 8.75. Check with the inverse: 8.75 + 6.25 = 15.
Line up the decimal points. Write 4.2 as 4.200 so every place has a digit. 4.200 − 1.375 = 2.825. Check with the inverse: 2.825 + 1.375 = 4.2.
Line up the decimal points. Write 23.6 as 23.600 so every place has a digit. 23.600 + 8.475 = 32.075.
Line up the decimal points. Write 6.4 as 6.40 so every place has a digit. 6.40 − 1.27 = 5.13. Check with the inverse: 5.13 + 1.27 = 6.4.
Line up the decimal points. Write 0.9 as 0.90 so every place has a digit. 0.90 + 0.25 = 1.15.
Write 1 as 1.00. 1.00 − 0.37 = 0.63. Check: 0.37 + 0.63 = 1.00. The hundredths make 10, so the tenths only need to make 9. (0.73 makes each digit up to 10.)
Write 1 as 1.00. 1.00 − 0.45 = 0.55. Check: 0.55 + 0.45 = 1. (0.65 makes each digit up to 10, but the tenths only need to make 9.)
Line up the points and fill the empty places: 2.50 + 1.75 + 0.80. Hundredths: 5. Tenths: 5 + 7 + 8 = 20, write 0, exchange 2 ones. Ones: 2 + 1 + 0 + 2 = 5. Answer: 5.05.
Use the inverse: the missing number is 4.85 + 2.6. 4.85 + 2.60 = 7.45. Check: 7.45 − 2.6 = 4.85.
3 tenths × 4 = 12 tenths. 10 tenths make 1 one, so 12 tenths = 1.2.
6 tenths × 5 = 30 tenths. 10 tenths make 1 one, so 30 tenths = 3.
8 hundredths × 7 = 56 hundredths = 0.56.
4 hundredths × 3 = 12 hundredths. 10 hundredths make 1 tenth, so the answer is 0.12.
Tenths: 4 × 3 = 12. Write 2, exchange 1 one. Ones: 1 × 3 + 1 = 4. Write 4. The point goes straight below the point: 4.2.
Tenths: 6 × 4 = 24. Write 4, exchange 2 ones. Ones: 2 × 4 + 2 = 10. Write 10. The point goes straight below the point: 10.4.
Tenths: 7 × 6 = 42. Write 2, exchange 4 ones. Ones: 3 × 6 + 4 = 22. Write 22. The point goes straight below the point: 22.2.
Tenths: 8 × 7 = 56. Write 6, exchange 5 ones. Ones: 5 × 7 + 5 = 40. Write 40. The point goes straight below the point: 40.6.

items.q: Use short multiplication. What is 2.45 × 6?
items.e: Hundredths: 5 × 6 = 30. Write 0, exchange 3 tenths. Tenths: 4 × 6 + 3 = 27. Write 7, exchange 2 ones. Ones: 2 × 6 + 2 = 14. Write 14. The point goes straight below the point: 14.70 = 14.7.

items.q: Use short multiplication. What is 1.36 × 4?
items.e: Hundredths: 6 × 4 = 24. Write 4, exchange 2 tenths. Tenths: 3 × 4 + 2 = 14. Write 4, exchange 1 one. Ones: 1 × 4 + 1 = 5. Write 5. The point goes straight below the point: 5.44.

items.q: Use short multiplication. What is 3.25 × 8?
items.e: Hundredths: 5 × 8 = 40. Write 0, exchange 4 tenths. Tenths: 2 × 8 + 4 = 20. Write 0, exchange 2 ones. Ones: 3 × 8 + 2 = 26. Write 26. The point goes straight below the point: 26.00 = 26.

items.q: Use short multiplication. What is 4.07 × 5?
items.e: Hundredths: 7 × 5 = 35. Write 5, exchange 3 tenths. Tenths: 0 × 5 + 3 = 3. Write 3. Ones: 4 × 5 = 20. Write 20. The point goes straight below the point: 20.35.

items.q: Use short multiplication. What is 6.78 × 3?
items.e: Hundredths: 8 × 3 = 24. Write 4, exchange 2 tenths. Tenths: 7 × 3 + 2 = 23. Write 3, exchange 2 ones. Ones: 6 × 3 + 2 = 20. Write 20. The point goes straight below the point: 20.34.

items.q: Use short multiplication. What is 9.15 × 4?
items.e: Hundredths: 5 × 4 = 20. Write 0, exchange 2 tenths. Tenths: 1 × 4 + 2 = 6. Write 6. Ones: 9 × 4 = 36. Write 36. The point goes straight below the point: 36.60 = 36.6.

items.q: 136 × 4 = 544. Use this to work out 1.36 × 4.

items.e: 0.37 is 37 ÷ 100, so 0.37 × 6 = 222 ÷ 100 = 2.22. Estimate: 0.37 is less than a half, and half of 6 is 3, so the answer is less than 3.
Partition 12 into 10 and 2. 0.75 × 10 = 7.5 and 0.75 × 2 = 1.5. 7.5 + 1.5 = 9. (7.5 forgets the 0.75 × 2 part. Or: three quarters of 12 is 9.)
Partition 25 into 20 and 5. 4.6 × 20 = 92 and 4.6 × 5 = 23. 92 + 23 = 115. (92 forgets the 4.6 × 5 part.)

items.q: Which is the best estimate for 3.92 × 7?
items.e: Round 3.92 to the nearest whole number: 4. Then 4 × 7 = 28. The exact answer is 27.44.

items.q: Which calculation has the same answer as 2.45 × 6?

sets.title: Divide with decimal answers and round

items.q: Use short division. What is 8.4 ÷ 4?
items.e: 8 ÷ 4 = 2; 4 ÷ 4 = 1. Keep the point in line: 8.4 ÷ 4 = 2.1.

items.q: Use short division. What is 9.36 ÷ 3?
Use short division. What is 7.38 ÷ 6?
Use short division. What is 4.08 ÷ 4?
17 ÷ 4 = ? Give your answer as a decimal.
items.e: Write 17 as 17.00 (the grey zeros). 17 ÷ 4 = 4 r 1. Exchange the 1 for 10 tenths: 10 ÷ 4 = 2 r 2. Exchange the 2 tenths for 20 hundredths: 20 ÷ 4 = 5. Answer: 4.25. (4.1 writes the remainder 1 as a decimal, but r 1 means 1 left over out of 4, which is 0.25.)
2 ÷ 8 = 0 r 2; 24 ÷ 8 = 3. Keep the point in line: 2.4 ÷ 8 = 0.3.

items.q: 13 ÷ 5 = ? Give your answer as a decimal.
items.e: Write 13 as 13.0 so you can keep dividing. 13 ÷ 5 = 2 r 3; 30 ÷ 5 = 6. Keep the point in line: 13 ÷ 5 = 2.6. (Not 2.3: the remainder is not the decimal part.)

items.q: 23 ÷ 4 = ? Give your answer as a decimal.
items.e: Write 23 as 23.00 so you can keep dividing. 23 ÷ 4 = 5 r 3; 30 ÷ 4 = 7 r 2; 20 ÷ 4 = 5. Keep the point in line: 23 ÷ 4 = 5.75. (Not 5.3: the remainder is not the decimal part.)

items.q: 12 ÷ 8 = ? Give your answer as a decimal.
items.e: Write 12 as 12.0 so you can keep dividing. 12 ÷ 8 = 1 r 4; 40 ÷ 8 = 5. Keep the point in line: 12 ÷ 8 = 1.5. (Not 1.4: the remainder is not the decimal part.)

items.q: 47 ÷ 5 = ? Give your answer as a decimal.
items.e: Write 47 as 47.0 so you can keep dividing. 47 ÷ 5 = 9 r 2; 20 ÷ 5 = 4. Keep the point in line: 47 ÷ 5 = 9.4. (Not 9.2: the remainder is not the decimal part.)

items.q: 39 ÷ 6 = ? Give your answer as a decimal.
items.e: Write 39 as 39.0 so you can keep dividing. 39 ÷ 6 = 6 r 3; 30 ÷ 6 = 5. Keep the point in line: 39 ÷ 6 = 6.5. (Not 6.3: the remainder is not the decimal part.)

items.q: 58 ÷ 8 = ? Give your answer as a decimal.
items.e: Write 58 as 58.00 so you can keep dividing. 58 ÷ 8 = 7 r 2; 20 ÷ 8 = 2 r 4; 40 ÷ 8 = 5. Keep the point in line: 58 ÷ 8 = 7.25. (Not 7.2: the remainder is not the decimal part.)

items.q: Round 3.45 to 1 decimal place.
items.e: 3.45 is between 3.4 and 3.5. Look at the hundredths digit: 5. 5 or more rounds up, so the answer is 3.5. 3.45 is exactly halfway, and halfway rounds up.

items.q: Round 14.27 to 1 decimal place.
items.e: 14.27 is between 14.2 and 14.3. The hundredths digit is 7, so round up: 14.3.

items.q: 20 ÷ 3 = ? Round your answer to 1 decimal place.
items.e: 20 ÷ 3 = 6.66… (work out one more place than you need). The hundredths digit is 6, so round up: 6.7. (6.6 just stops; it does not round.)

items.q: 10 ÷ 6 = ? Round your answer to 1 decimal place.
items.e: 10 ÷ 6 = 1.66… (work out one more place than you need). The hundredths digit is 6, so round up: 1.7.

items.q: 25 ÷ 6 = ? Round your answer to 1 decimal place.
items.e: 25 ÷ 6 = 4.16… (work out one more place than you need). The hundredths digit is 6, so round up: 4.2.

items.q: 50 ÷ 7 = ? Round your answer to the nearest whole number.
items.e: 50 ÷ 7 = 7.1… (work out one more place than you need). The tenths digit is 1, so round down: 7. (1 is the remainder, not the answer.)

items.q: Evie buys 4 notebooks for £1.35 each. How much does she spend?
items.e: £1.35 × 4. Hundredths: 5 × 4 = 20. Write 0, exchange 2 tenths. Tenths: 3 × 4 + 2 = 14. Write 4, exchange 1 one. Ones: 1 × 4 + 1 = 5. Write 5. Keep the point in line: she spends £5.40.

items.q: Alfie has £12.50. He spends £3.78 on a book. How much money does he have left?
Four friends share a restaurant bill of £47.60 equally. How much does each person pay?
£20 is shared equally between 3 children. How much does each child get, to the nearest penny?
items.e: 20 ÷ 3 = 6.666… The nearest penny is 2 decimal places. Look at the third decimal place: 6, so round up. Each child gets £6.67. (£6.66 just stops; £6.20 writes the remainder 2 as 20p.)

items.q: Zara cuts a 3.6 m ribbon into 8 equal pieces. How long is each piece?
items.e: 3.6 ÷ 8: 8 does not go into 3, so write 0. 36 tenths ÷ 8 = 4 r 4. Exchange the 4 tenths for 40 hundredths: 40 ÷ 8 = 5. Each piece is 0.45 m (45 cm). (0.44 m writes the remainder 4 as the next digit.)

items.q: A bag of apples has a mass of 1.25 kg. What is the mass of 6 bags?
items.e: 1.25 × 6. Hundredths: 5 × 6 = 30. Write 0, exchange 3 tenths. Tenths: 2 × 6 + 3 = 15. Write 5, exchange 1 one. Ones: 1 × 6 + 1 = 7. Write 7. Keep the point in line: 7.50 kg. The 6 bags have a mass of 7.5 kg.

items.q: In the long jump, Jack jumps 3.2 m and Poppy jumps 2.85 m. How much further does Jack jump?
A pack of 100 pencils costs £18. How much is one pencil?
items.e: £18 ÷ 100: the digits move 2 places to the right, so one pencil costs £0.18 = 18p. (£1.80 is £18 ÷ 10.)

items.q: A cycle path is 4.5 km long. How many metres is that?
items.e: 1 km = 1,000 m, so multiply by 1,000. The digits move 3 places to the left: 4.5 × 1,000 = 4,500 m.

items.q: 7 friends share a £45.50 bill equally. How much does each pay?
items.e: 45.50 ÷ 7: 45 ÷ 7 = 6 r 3. Exchange the 3 for 30 tenths, with the 5 tenths that makes 35 tenths: 35 ÷ 7 = 5. 0 ÷ 7 = 0. Each pays £6.50. (£6.30 writes the remainder 3 as 30p.)

items.q: Amelia cuts 8 m of rope into 3 equal pieces. How long is each piece, to 1 decimal place?
items.e: 8 ÷ 3 = 2.66… To round to 1 decimal place, look at the hundredths digit: 6, so round up. Each piece is 2.7 m. (2.2 m writes the remainder 2 as a decimal.)

items.q: Freya buys 3 bottles of juice at £1.49 each. She pays with a £5 note. How much change does she get?
A box of 6 eggs costs £1.86. How much does one egg cost?
A sunflower grows from 0.85 m to 1.6 m tall. How much does it grow?
One lap of the school field is 0.4 km. Kai runs 7 laps. How far does he run?
items.e: 4 tenths × 7 = 28 tenths = 2.8 km.

items.q: A taxi fare of £17.30 is shared equally by 4 people. How much does each person pay, to the nearest penny?
items.e: 17.30 ÷ 4 = 4.325. The third decimal place is 5, so round up to the nearest penny: £4.33. (£4.32 just stops; £4.30 is rounded to the nearest 10p, not the nearest penny.)

items.q: One sheet of paper has a mass of 4.5 g. What is the mass of 1,000 sheets in kilograms?
Paint costs £2.35 per litre. How much do 5 litres cost?
items.e: £2.35 × 5. Hundredths: 5 × 5 = 25. Write 5, exchange 2 tenths. Tenths: 3 × 5 + 2 = 17. Write 7, exchange 1 one. Ones: 2 × 5 + 1 = 11. Write 11. Keep the point in line: 5 litres cost £11.75.

items.q: Isla buys a drink for 65p, a sandwich for £1.20 and an apple for 80p. How much does she spend?
items.e: Write everything in pounds: £0.65 + £1.20 + £0.80. Line up the points: 0.65 + 1.20 + 0.80 = £2.65. (£146 adds 65 + 1 + 80 without changing the pence into pounds; £1.93 writes 80p as £0.08.)

items.q: A 2.5 litre bottle of water is poured equally into 4 jugs. How much is in each jug, to 1 decimal place?
items.e: 2.5 ÷ 4 = 0.625. To round to 1 decimal place, look at the hundredths digit: 2, so round down. Each jug has about 0.6 litres. (0.62 and 0.625 are not rounded to 1 decimal place.)
